name: Belgium

tax_year.return_due: Income of 2026 goes in the 2027 return; the 2027 dates were not yet published, and in 2026 they were 30 June on paper and 19 July online.

summary: A Belgian bank withholds 30% on most dividends and interest (roerende voorheffing), and that settles the tax. Since 1 January 2026, profits on shares, funds, bonds and crypto are taxed at 10%, with the first €10,000 of gains a year tax-free per person. Buying and selling securities also costs a stock-exchange tax, and securities accounts worth more than €1 million on average pay a yearly tax.

topics.title: Profit when you sell
points: Since 1 January 2026, profits on financial assets are taxed at 10% (meerwaardebelasting). This covers shares, bonds, ETFs and other funds, options, savings and investment insurance, currency and crypto, Belgian or foreign.
The gain is the sale price minus the purchase price. Costs and taxes cannot be deducted.

For assets bought before 2026, the purchase price is their value on 31 December 2025. If you paid more than that, you may use your original price, but a loss compared with that original price cannot be deducted.
Leaving Belgium can trigger an exit tax on gains not yet realised.

topics.title: Dividends
points: Most dividends are taxed at 30%. A Belgian bank withholds this and it is the final tax; you do not need to declare those dividends.
The first €833 of ordinary dividends per person is tax-free. Belgian banks still withhold tax on it, so you reclaim it in your return (codes 1437/2437), up to €249.90.
Dividends from investment funds do not get this exemption.

topics.title: Interest on savings
points: Most interest is taxed at 30%, withheld by a Belgian bank.
On a regulated savings account (gereglementeerde spaarrekening), the first €1,020 of interest per person is tax-free, and interest above that is taxed at 15%.
Interest from a foreign bank has no Belgian tax withheld, so you must declare it in your return.

figures.label: Tax-free interest on regulated savings, per person

topics.title: Funds and ETFs
points: Funds and trackers (ETFs) fall under the 10% tax on gains when you sell them.
Dividends paid by funds do not get the €833 dividend exemption.
Buying or selling fund units also pays the stock-exchange tax; the rate depends on the type of security (see What your broker does).

topics.title: Tax on what you own
points: There is a yearly tax on securities accounts (effectentaks) whose average value over the reference period, normally 1 October to 30 September, is more than €1 million.

The rate is 0.15% for periods ending up to 31 May 2026 and 0.30% for periods ending from 1 June 2026. A Belgian bank withholds and files it; where the holder must file it, the deadline is 15 July of the following year.

topics.title: Tax-free amounts
points: Gains: the first €10,000 of gains a year is tax-free (for income of 2026). If you do not use it, up to €1,000 of it carries to the next year, for up to five years, to a maximum of €15,000.
Dividends: the first €833 a year is tax-free. Interest on regulated savings accounts: the first €1,020 a year is tax-free.
These amounts are per person, so each partner in a couple has their own.

topics.title: Tax-free and tax-deferred accounts
points: Pension saving (pensioensparen) gives a tax reduction: 30% of up to €1,050 paid in 2026, or 25% of up to €1,350. Only one contract per person counts each year.
Pension saving accounts, group insurance and long-term saving contracts are exempt from the new tax on gains. Payouts have their own tax rules, not covered here.

topics.title: Losses
points: Under certain conditions, losses realised in a year can be deducted from that year's taxable gains.
Losses that arose before 2026 cannot be deducted: if a holding bought earlier is sold below its original price, the result counts as zero.

topics.title: Foreign shares
points: As a resident you declare your income from anywhere in the world.

Tax withheld abroad on a dividend is not Belgian tax and is not credited. You declare the dividend after the foreign tax, and Belgium then taxes it at 30%; the first €833 of ordinary dividends is tax-free.
Accounts abroad must be reported to the Central Point of Contact (CAP) of the National Bank and in your tax return.

topics.title: What your broker does and what you do
points: A Belgian bank or broker withholds 30% on dividends and interest. For gains it withholds 10% by default (opt in); exempt gains can be reclaimed in your return. If you opt out, nothing is withheld, you declare the gains yourself, and the bank reports them to the tax office.
A foreign broker withholds no Belgian tax. You declare dividends and interest above the exemptions and your gains in the return, and report the account to the National Bank.

Each trade pays the stock-exchange tax (taks op de beursverrichtingen) of 0.12%, 0.35% or 1.32% depending on the security, capped at €1,300, €1,600 or €4,000 per trade. With a foreign broker that does not pay it for you, you file and pay it yourself in MyMinfin by the last working day of the second month after the trade.

topics.title: Crypto
points: Crypto is listed as a financial asset, so gains on it are taxed at 10% from 2026 under the same rules and yearly exemption as shares.
